router_body:
name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: full job set selected
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: echo 'SELECTED gauntlet sessions tier'
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
      - name: local gate wiring proof
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: python3 -I ci/local-gate-test.py
      - name: local evidence gate
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix')) }}
        run: echo 'Local gauntlet evidence is the gate; request ci or full-matrix for CI.'

ci.yml.gauntlet:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'gauntlet')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The legs are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): each host on each
        # compiler tier, `tier: native` and `tier: release` (pelt#40: one job
        # ran both tiers' corpus and sessions, 38-41 of macOS's 45 minutes).
        # Linux x86-64, macOS arm64 and linux aarch64 (`builds: false`, where
        # the job asserts the tier is refused by name, wolf-lang#614) in the
        # all tier (the nightly); the same but macOS's release leg in the
        # full tier (the merge; tl30, the macOS cap); linux x86-64 alone in
        # a pull request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_gauntlet || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # pelt#99 (sh34): the session corpus is the `sessions` job's since the
    # friendly campaign doubled it (290 cases, 590 s on macOS, to 584 and
    # 1,500 s): the whole leg's peak steps summed to 47-50 minutes on macOS,
    # past this job's old 45. Without them this job's peak is 24.6 minutes
    # (macOS release, the ten nightlies to 2026-11-01); the limit is the
    # house rule's: (peak + 180 s) x 1.4, 38.7, so 40.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: wolf fmt --check
        # Once a host, on the native leg: it needs no build and no tier.
        if: matrix.tier == 'native'
        run: tools/check-fmt

      # sh06: tests/census/clauses.tsv lists POSIX.1-2024's testable
      # statements and the cases that show each. The table must agree
      # with the tree (every case it names exists, every census case is
      # named); it needs no built pelt, so every host checks it.
      - name: the clause table agrees with the corpus
        # Once a host, on the native leg: it needs no build and no tier.
        if: matrix.tier == 'native'
        run: tools/clause-census

      # sh11: the line editor's width table is what tools/gen-width
      # makes from Unicode 16.0.0. A runner whose Python carries another
      # Unicode version says so here rather than in a session.
      - name: the width table is the generated one
        # Once a host, on the native leg: it needs no build and no tier.
        if: matrix.tier == 'native'
        run: |
          python3 -c "import unicodedata; print('runner Unicode', unicodedata.unidata_version)"
          if python3 -c "import unicodedata, sys; sys.exit(unicodedata.unidata_version != '16.0.0')"; then
            tools/gen-width --check
          else
            echo "::notice::runner Python is not Unicode 16.0.0; the table is checked on kasumi (notes/sh11-the-line-editor.md)"
          fi

      - name: build, the ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: matrix.builds
        run: tools/build --${{ matrix.tier }}

      - name: the ${{ matrix.tier }} tier is refused on this host, by name (wolf-lang#614)
        if: ${{ !matrix.builds }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          TIER: ${{ matrix.tier }}
        run: |
          set +e
          tools/build --"$TIER" >"$TIER.log" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          cat "$TIER.log"
          if [ "$code" = 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::the $TIER tier now builds on linux aarch64; widen the matrix"
            exit 1
          fi
          grep -q "this host cannot run the $TIER tier" "$TIER.log"

      - name: wolf test (the table checks)
        # tools/check-test runs the unit tests, once a host on the native
        # leg; `wolf test` runs them on the checked machine (its rows are
        # `unsupported` where that machine refuses a construct), so the
        # compiled tiers run the same checks below (`tools/self-check`, sh20).
        if: matrix.builds && matrix.tier == 'native'
        run: tools/check-test

      # sh20: the table checks again, on the tier just built (`wolf test`
      # above runs them on the checked machine), with the one row only a
      # compiled tier can answer: a fork asked while a task is live is
      # answered `busy`, and pelt runs the shape in process, as it does on
      # a host that does not fork (pelt starts no task; src/sh/fork.lu;
      # the task is src/selfcheck.lu's, a program of its own).
      - name: the table checks on the ${{ matrix.tier }} tier, busy's row with them
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/self-check ${{ matrix.tier }}

      # pelt#3: a word that is not a pattern (`[`, `a]`, `[a`) reads no
      # directory. End to end: a `[ … ]` loop's peak RSS in a directory
      # of 64 files must match an empty directory's (tools/glob-rss).
      # It runs even when `wolf test` is red, so the table check's count
      # and this measurement each report on their own.
      - name: no directory read for a non-pattern word, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/glob-rss target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # wolf-lang#612, sh03: each command's scratch dies with it
      # (`copy region`), so a loop of commands keeps only what it
      # assigns. s216's loop at 10,000 and 20,000 turns; the larger may
      # peak at most 100 bytes a turn (plus 1 MiB) above the smaller
      # (tools/loop-rss; pelt before sh03 grew 7.4 KB a turn).
      - name: memory flat over a loop of commands, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/loop-rss target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # pelt#19, sh08: and over every other shape a long script or session
      # repeats — a pipeline, a command substitution, a subshell, a
      # function call (with `local` and `return`), an arithmetic
      # assignment, `case` and `for`, a script of 10,000 and 20,000
      # lines, and lines typed at the prompt — each at 10,000 and 20,000
      # turns under loop-rss's bound (100 B a turn + 1 MiB). Before sh08
      # 21 of the 22 rows failed, growing 0.35 to 13.5 KB a turn; the
      # 22nd is the bare loop, for scale (tools/shape-rss). sh19 (pelt#33)
      # added `wait`, `export`, `kill`, and `cmd & wait` in a loop, a
      # script and at the prompt, which kept 600 to 2,300 B a turn before.
      # sh22 (pelt#39) added `read` with a redirection, `eval`, `cd .`,
      # `command`, `umask` and a job nobody waits for, which kept 131 to
      # 1,700 B a turn. sh20 (pelt#34) added the shapes that fork, a
      # process a turn: a substitution and a subshell of two commands, a
      # brace group and a subshell after `&`, a stage pelt runs itself, in
      # a loop, a script and at the prompt.
      - name: memory flat over every shape, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: tools/shape-rss target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # sh05: `exec cmd` replaces the shell (`os_exec`). The corpus sees
      # only what a script prints, and a shell that ran the program as
      # a child and then left would print the same; this asks the host:
      # the same pid becomes the program, with no child under it, the
      # environment handed over is exactly the exported variables, a
      # descriptor the shell opened is the program's, and a death by
      # signal reaches the shell's parent as one (tools/exec-witness).
      - name: exec replaces the shell (same pid), ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/exec-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # sh14: a trap's action runs when the command the signal came
      # during ends, asked 5,000 times with a child as the sender and
      # 5,000 with the shell's own `kill` (before wolf 0.2.29 a poll
      # could trail a delivery, wolf-lang#691, and pelt carried a
      # barrier; trunk without it missed 3 to 12 of 5,000,
      # notes/sh14-evidence/logs/red-barrier.log). And a shell started
      # with signals ignored neither traps nor resets them, asked from
      # outside (the corpus harness starts every case with the
      # defaults) (tools/signal-witness).
      - name: traps run on time; ignored at start stays ignored, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: tools/signal-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # The corpus steps run whatever came before, so that a break seen
      # only from outside (above) and one seen only by a script each
      # report on their own; so does every step after them.
      - name: the differential corpus, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/difftest --bin target/${{ matrix.tier }}

      - name: the harness sees a difference (the planted red)
        # The release leg's: the selftest runs the release build.
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && matrix.tier == 'release' && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/difftest-selftest target/release

      - name: shadow bytes, bounded lookup and idle, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: tools/shadow-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      - name: colour bytes, reset boundaries and idle, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: tools/colour-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      - name: words witness loader and fixture contracts
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 tools/words-loader-test

      - name: words bytes, abbreviation isolation and bounded pager, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: tools/words-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      - name: prompt bytes, precedence, VCS deadline and idle, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: tools/prompt-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # sh11: the editor gives the terminal back, asked from outside: the
      # modes after SIGHUP (pelt dies of it, as dash), SIGTERM (ignored),
      # SIGINT (the line abandoned, $? 130) and a hangup (tools/edit-witness).
      # sh15 (wolf 0.2.30): IXON and IEXTEN off while a line is edited,
      # no context switch at an idle prompt (the editor waits in
      # os_signal_wait_fd; a VTIME read made about ten a second), a
      # `kill -INT` answered at once, a resize redrawn mid-line.
      # sh16: Tab at an empty command name (every PATH directory read)
      # rings within half a second, and the next Tab asks before a list.
      # Every session above also fails if pelt exits with the terminal's
      # ICANON, ECHO, ISIG, IEXTEN or IXON changed.
      - name: the editor restores the terminal, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: tools/edit-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # sh12: the history file, asked from outside (one session is one
      # shell): written as typed and read by the next shell, two shells
      # sharing one file, the file kept to HISTSIZE, a path that cannot
      # be made and a file that is not text left alone, $HOME/.sh_history
      # made 0600 (tools/hist-witness).
      - name: the history file across shells, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: tools/hist-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}/pelt

      # pelt#27, sh22: a harness whose case times out ends everything the
      # case started (tools/lib_reap.py), asked from outside: tests/reap's
      # one case times out on purpose with a child, a job in a group of
      # its own and the job's child, through tools/difftest and, on linux,
      # under tools/syscall-census, whose timeout used to end `strace` and
      # leave the shell it followed running (sh14 found three on kasumi).
      # strace is the census row's; the linux runners do not carry it.
      - name: strace, for the census row (linux)
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && runner.os == 'Linux' && !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          if ! command -v strace; then
            sudo apt-get update -qq
            sudo apt-get install -y -qq strace
          fi

      - name: a case that times out leaves nothing running, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && !cancelled() }}
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: tools/reap-witness target/${{ matrix.tier }}


  # The prompt: sessions typed into pelt through a pseudo-terminal and
  # compared with transcripts tools/session-record wrote from `dash -i +m`
  # (tests/session/, tools/lib_session.py), on every leg that builds, each
  # host on each compiler tier as the gauntlet's. pelt#99 (sh34): its own
  # job since the friendly campaign doubled the corpus (584 cases; 1,500 s
  # on macOS, 1,245 s on linux), so the two run side by side and each fits
  # its limit with room. Limits by the house rule, (peak + 180 s) x 1.4,
  # over the ten nightlies to 2026-11-01 plus sh34's eight cases: the job's
  # peak 27.5 minutes (macOS release), 42.7, so 45; the corpus's own step
  # 25.1 minutes on macOS, 39.8, so 40, and 20.7 on linux, 33.6, so 35.
  # No case is skipped, filtered or sharded.
ci.yml.sessions:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'sessions')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The plan's legs (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): the gauntlet's that build,
        # linux x86-64 and macOS arm64 on each compiler tier, in the all
        # tier; all but macOS's release leg in the full tier; linux x86-64
        # alone in a pull request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_sessions || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: build, the ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        run: tools/build --${{ matrix.tier }}

      # The prompt: sessions typed into pelt through a pseudo-terminal
      # and compared with transcripts tools/session-record wrote from
      # `dash -i +m` (tests/session/, tools/lib_session.py).
      # pelt#35, sh19: a break the sessions see is seen whatever the
      # corpus said (a plant whose corpus was red once never showed its
      # sessions, sh18's run 39160267977); in a job of their own since
      # sh34 they wait on nothing but this leg's build.
      # sh29: run 40160785846 reached about 408 sessions without a failure
      # before macOS native exhausted the old 15-minute step cap; sh34
      # (pelt#99) sizes the step by the house rule, above the job.
      - name: the session corpus, ${{ matrix.tier }} tier
        timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.os == 'macos-latest' && 40 || 35 }}
        run: tools/session --bin target/${{ matrix.tier }}

      - name: the session harness sees a difference (the planted red)
        # The release leg's: the selftest runs the release build.
        if: ${{ matrix.tier == 'release' && !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/session-selftest target/release

  # The run's verdict, and its name: `tier full`, `tier pr` or `tier noop`.
  # It needs every job, runs unless the run was cancelled, and fails unless
  # the plan succeeded, the hosts it chose are the tier's, every
  # chosen job succeeded and every other job was skipped (ci/tiers.py
  # verdict). lane-audit.sh reads this job's name and conclusion.
ci.yml.tier:
name: tier ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tier || 'unplanned' }}
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs:
      - plan
      - gauntlet
      - sessions
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: every chosen job succeeded, every other was skipped
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 ci/tiers.py verdict

  # A red nightly opens an issue (ruling #92): a scheduled run has no lane
  # watching it, so the red has to come and find one. One open issue per
  # workflow, its title the dedupe key; a further red night comments on it
  # (ci/nightly-red.sh, tested by ci/tiers-test.py T8). Never on a pull
  # request, a push or a dispatch: those reds have a lane attached already.
ci.yml.nightly-red:
name: nightly red, an issue
    needs: tier
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: open or update the nightly-red issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: ci/nightly-red.sh
